There's a lot in the Bible about love, respect, and mutual support. For example, Ephesians 5 talks about husbands loving their wives as Christ loved the church, and wives submitting to their husbands. But submission doesn't mean doing everything the husband says without question; it's more about mutual respect and working together as a team. So, in this scenario, the woman didn't cook because her husband said he'd be late. Is that a problem? Maybe she could have prepared something simple or maybe he would have preferred having dinner ready despite the delay. I'm also thinking about communication. Did she talk to her husband about why she didn't cook? Maybe she assumed he wouldn't want dinner, but perhaps he would have appreciated it. Good communication is important in a marriage, and maybe she could have discussed it instead of making the decision on her own. On the flip side, maybe she felt that her time was valuable and that she deserved a break. It's important for both partners to contribute and support each other. If she usually does all the cooking, maybe this was her way of taking a step back and expecting her husband to help out more. But then, is that the right approach without discussing it first? I'm also considering the idea of priorities. If she didn't cook because she had other things to do, that's one thing. But if it's because she felt her husband's schedule was more important, that might not be the best approach. Both partners should feel valued and supported. In the end, I'm leaning towards it being wrong because it might not reflect the biblical principles of love, service, and mutual respect.
